text:
anya: Hey team — just opened a PR to add the novum9b model card + SDK v4 migration snippets. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4921 Preview: https://deploy-preview.example/4921. Adds supported_variants, quantization_profiles, sequence limits (8k/16k), and a short throughput section. Looking for quick QA + docs review.

mike: cool. can we include p50/p90 tokens/sec for both 8k and 16k profiles? engineering wants numbers to cite in the card. also please add a Node streaming example — we have more Node users.

anya: added microbench numbers: 8k p50 480 tok/s @A100-80GB, p90 360 tok/s; 16k p50 210 tok/s, p90 160 tok/s. noted var when mixed-batch padding is enabled (~10% drop). added Node streaming snippet.

rio: quick schema nit: in model-card frontmatter you used "max_seq_len" but our catalog schema requires "max_sequence_length". Linter will fail on CI.

anya: fixed to "max_sequence_length" and pushed. thanks.

samir: can we add a short CPU-quant fallback paragraph? Ops needs guidance for small VMs. Call out recommended quant_profile names and expected perf hit.

anya: added CPU fallback section — recommended quant_profile: "cpu-int8" or "cpu-quant" for single-socket 4GB VMs. noted: expect ~2-3x latency increase vs GPU and potential tokenization differences for short prefixes. linked to bench artifact: https://bench.internal/novum9b/4921

jenna: link check: the quant_profiles anchor 404s in the docs nav. anchor in the content points to "#quantization_profiles" but site uses dashed anchors like "#quantization-profiles". small fix needed.

anya: fixed anchor to "#quantization-profiles" and updated TOC entry. pushed.

mike: @samir can you sign off on quality language for CPU fallback? we should avoid strong claims about generation quality.

samir: LGTM with softer language — changed "affects output" to "may alter short-token choices; recommend eval on key prompt set". also left a short eval command linking to our eval harness.

anya: added Node + Python snippets in a new "Examples" subsection. Python streaming snippet: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
for chunk in client.generate("novum9b", input="Summarize: ...", stream=True).stream():
    print(chunk.text, end="")
```
Node streaming snippet: ```js
const { Client } = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const stream = client.generate({ model: 'novum9b', input: 'Hello', stream: true });
for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk.text); }
```

Added an embeddings fallback example for CPU-only: set `variant: "sparse-lite"` or `quant_profile: "cpu-int8"` and call out lower throughput.

docs-bot: preview build succeeded ✅ — staging URL: https://staging.docs.redwood.ai/preview/4921. Lint: 1 warning (internal link style) resolved.

mike: one last ask — can we add a short migration checklist in the PR description so engineers know which model fields changed (e.g., max_sequence_length key rename, new quant_profile enum)?

anya: added a migration checklist + changelog bullet. requesting final approvals from @mike @jenna @samir. will merge after approvals. :rocket:
